key: A food critic who has eaten everywhere
name: ch00_food_critic_new_taste
alt: A seasoned food critic tastes a long row of familiar dishes with a bored face, then lights up at the one plate he has never tasted before.
scene: A wide, warm interior of a small Indian restaurant at lunchtime, seen from table height. In the centre sits a grey-haired food critic in his sixties, round glasses, cream kurta with a notebook and pen beside his plate, a napkin tucked in at the collar. In front of him a long table is lined left to right with eight small steel katoris: dal, paneer, a plain curry, another curry that looks almost the same, rice, a familiar dessert. Above the first seven bowls, tiny thought bubbles from his head show the same plate he has eaten before, each with a small tick, and his expression over them is polite and bored, chin resting on one hand. At the far right end sits one unusual dish in a banana leaf, steam curling up in a different colour, and here his eyebrows rise, his spoon is lifted halfway to his mouth, and his notebook pen is already moving. A young waiter in a black waistcoat stands in the background left, watching anxiously with a tray under his arm; through the window behind, a busy street with a scooter passing. Soft daylight from the window, a quietly humorous mood. Labels: "SEEN IT" in small letters floating above the row of ordinary bowls, "NEW" above the banana-leaf dish on the right.

key: Two runners in the same marathon need
name: ch00_runners_borrowed_shoes
alt: A tall marathon winner hands his large running shoes to a shorter friend whose feet slip and blister inside them.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, set at the finish area of a city marathon with marigold garlands on the barriers and a banner with no words. LEFT panel: a tall, lean runner in his thirties, sweat-soaked orange vest and a finisher medal round his neck, grins as he unlaces a pair of large running shoes and holds them out to his shorter friend; an inset bubble shows the shoes fitting his own long feet snugly. RIGHT panel: the friend, a stocky man in his forties with a bandana and a blue vest, is now running in those same shoes; they are visibly too long, the toes flap, the heels slip out with each stride, and a small red blister glows on his heel in a circular close-up inset. He winces and has dropped behind other runners who pass him easily in their own fitted shoes. A dotted arrow travels from the shoes in the left panel to his feet on the right, showing that the same pair moved owners. Morning light, long shadows across the road, a gently comic mood. Labels: "FITS HIM" under the winner in the left panel, "BLISTERS" under the friend's feet on the right.

key: Climate and weather. The season says
name: ch00_summer_season_storm_day
alt: On a bright summer calendar month, one day shows a sudden storm, and a man in summer clothes carries an umbrella without contradiction.
scene: A single scene on a sunny Indian residential street, with a large wall calendar painted on the side of a house filling the background left. The calendar shows a whole summer month of small sun icons, every square yellow, with one square circled in red where a small storm cloud sits; a long sun-coloured arrow runs across the top of the calendar pointing up-right. In the foreground right, the same street at this moment is under one dark, local storm cloud pouring rain onto a short stretch of pavement while the sky behind is still bright blue. A man in his thirties wearing half-sleeve linen shirt, shorts and sandals, clearly dressed for summer, stands under that cloud holding an open black umbrella, calm and dry, a mango in his other hand. A street dog shelters under a parked scooter beside him. A thin dotted line links the circled calendar square to the cloud above his head, showing that today's weather sits inside the summer season. Strong contrast between warm golden light on the calendar side and cool grey light under the cloud, cheerful rather than gloomy. Labels: "SEASON: UP" above the calendar, "TODAY: STORM" beside the rain cloud.

key: A poker player who buys in with the
name: ch00_poker_buyin_whole_vs_small
alt: One poker player pushes his entire bankroll in and is shown leaving broke, while another bets a tiny slice and is still seated when the cards turn.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle, both halves showing the same green-felt card table under a low hanging lamp. LEFT panel: a young man in his twenties, gold chain and loud shirt, has shoved a huge tower of chips and a fat bundle of cash into the middle, all of his money; the next frame within the panel, drawn smaller below like a strip, shows him walking out of the room with empty pockets turned inside out, head down, while the dealer rakes his whole pile away. RIGHT panel: a calm woman in her forties, spectacles and a plain grey cardigan, keeps a big stack of chips beside her and slides only one small chip forward; a small round gauge on the table edge shows a thin slice marked "2%". Below, a second smaller frame shows her still seated hours later, a clock on the wall moved on, a winning hand turned face up in front of her and the dealer pushing a pot her way. Thick arrows show the whole pile leaving in the left panel and a thin trickle leaving and a larger flow returning in the right panel. Dim, focused lamplight with deep shadows, tense in the left half and patient in the right. Labels: "ALL IN" at the top of the left panel, "STILL SEATED" at the top of the right panel.

key: A poker table. Every chip a player
name: ch00_poker_table_chips_and_rake
alt: Seen from above, chips flow from one player's stack to another across a card table, and the house takes a small cut from every pot.
scene: A top-down view looking straight down at an oval card table with green felt, six players seated around it, only their hands, forearms and chip stacks visible at the edges. In the very centre lies a pot of chips; curved arrows show chips sliding into the pot from four players and then a thick arrow carrying the whole pot to one winner's stack at the lower right, whose hands are gathering it in. A small brass dish at the dealer's position at the top edge catches a few chips taken from the pot with a little scoop, the house cut, and a thin arrow peels off the pot into that dish. The felt itself has a faint price chart printed on it like a pattern, a zig-zag line running across the table under the chips, which the players' hands ignore completely; they are all looking at one another's faces instead, drawn as small round head shapes at the table edge with watchful expressions. Overhead lamp light falls in a bright circle on the felt, the corners of the room dark. A serious, watchful mood. Labels: "RAKE" next to the brass dish, "JUST THE FELT" written small along the bottom edge of the table, "OTHER PLAYERS" near the chip stacks on the left.

key: A row of dominoes behind a door
name: ch00_dominoes_behind_door
alt: A hand pushes through a half-open door and topples a hidden row of dominoes, which fall until the row ends where a patient figure waits to collect them.
scene: A cutaway side view of a corridor with a closed wooden door on the left. The wall has been cut away so the viewer can see what the characters cannot: behind the door a long straight row of standing dominoes runs toward the right across a tiled floor. A heavy man's hand in a dark suit sleeve pushes through the door, which is opening a crack, and nudges the first domino; the first five are already falling in a curve of motion, each knocking the next, small impact stars between them. Above the row, a pencil line on the wall marks where the row begins, drawn by several small figures in the corridor outside who point at the door knowingly. At the far right end the row stops, the last domino has fallen flat, and a calm older woman in a green sari squats beside the heap with a cloth bag, picking up the fallen dominoes one by one with a quiet smile, a price tag reading "CHEAP" taped to the bag. A long arrow along the floor runs from the push to the end of the row. Soft side light from a corridor window, the hidden part slightly darker. Labels: "ONE BIG SELLER" by the pushing hand, "MOVE STOPS" where the row ends.

key: A field guide written by a local
name: ch00_local_field_guide
alt: A local boatman's hand-drawn guide points straight to the dangerous river bend and the safe landing, beside a thick unopened textbook on map reading.
scene: A riverside scene in the early morning at a ghat on a wide Indian river. In the foreground on a stone step lies a fat, heavy textbook with a plain cover and a bookmark at page one, its open page showing a generic compass and grid, gathering a little dust and a fallen leaf; nobody is using it. In the middle ground a weathered local boatman in his fifties, white vest, checked lungi and a towel over his shoulder, kneels beside a young traveller with a backpack and points with one finger at a small, worn notebook held open between them. The notebook page is hand-drawn: a sketch of this very river with a whirlpool marked in red at a bend and a green arrow to a sandy bank. Behind them, on the actual river, the same bend is visible with swirling dangerous water and rocks, and further along the safe sandy landing with two tied boats, matching the sketch. Dotted lines connect the sketch's whirlpool to the real whirlpool and the sketch's arrow to the real landing. Soft mist on the water, golden low sun, a calm, trusting mood. Labels: "THE BASICS" under the unused textbook, "WHERE IT IS DANGEROUS" beside the whirlpool, "LAND HERE" above the sandy bank.

key: A secret fishing spot. If it
name: ch00_fishing_pond_vs_ocean_bus
alt: A small pond is emptied by a few extra anglers, while a busload of anglers at the ocean barely changes the catch and most soon wander away.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a small village pond ringed by reeds, with one quiet angler in a straw hat who has been joined by four more people elbow to elbow; their buckets are full but the pond is clearly emptied, just two tiny fish left visible under the surface, and a little calendar inset shows only one season passing. RIGHT panel: a vast open sea from a rocky shore, waves rolling, huge shoals of fish visible as dark shapes under the water. A bright painted tourist bus is parked on the coast road, and twenty anglers have spilled out along the rocks with rods; the original angler, the same straw-hatted man, still catches fish at his usual spot as if nothing changed. On the right side of that panel most of the bus passengers are walking away after a couple of casts, rods over their shoulders, shrugging, heading toward other coves, with dotted footprints trailing off. Bright midday light, sea breeze, light-hearted mood. Labels: "SMALL POND" at the top of the left panel, "OCEAN" at the top of the right panel, "GAVE UP" near the anglers walking away.

key: Choosing a sport. A sprinter forced
name: ch00_sprinter_vs_marathoner_fit
alt: A muscular sprinter struggles exhausted in a marathon while a wiry marathoner trails far behind in a sprint, each in the wrong race.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle, both halves on athletic tracks. LEFT panel: a long road race through a city at the 30-kilometre marker, a muscular, broad-shouldered sprinter in a red vest and short spikes is bent double at the roadside, hands on knees, gasping and drenched, while lean distance runners stream past him at an easy pace. RIGHT panel: a 100-metre stadium straight, the finish tape just snapping; a thin, wiry marathon runner in a long-sleeve top and cushioned trainers is still only halfway down the lane, legs moving gracefully but far too slowly, while compact sprinters burst through the tape. Both athletes have determined, sweating faces: they are clearly trying hard. Between the two panels, in the centre at the bottom, an inset shows the two athletes swapping places, with curved arrows, the sprinter walking toward a stadium and the marathoner toward a long road, both now smiling. Bright, hot afternoon light on both tracks, a sympathetic mood. Labels: "WRONG RACE" at the top across both panels, "RIGHT FIT" under the bottom inset.

key: Boot camp before the battlefield
name: ch01_boot_camp_before_battle
alt: Recruits drill on a training ground studying a terrain model and a stress test, while a distant battlefield waits beyond the fence.
scene: A wide view of an army training ground at dawn, split into foreground and background by a wire fence with a gate. In the foreground left, a group of five young recruits in olive T-shirts and caps crowd around a sand-table model of hills, a river and roads, while a stern drill instructor in his forties with a moustache and a cane points at the ridge lines. In the foreground right, two other recruits do a stress drill: one crawls under netting while a whistle blows, the other stands blindfolded reassembling a rifle-shaped wooden block, his face strained and sweating, as a small thought bubble above him shows a tangle of scribbles for panic. Through the open gate in the background, far away on a hazy plain, the real battlefield waits: hills that match the sand table, smoke drifting, and a signpost pointing that way. A dotted arrow runs from the training ground through the gate toward the distant plain. Cool dawn light, dust in the air, disciplined and focused mood. Labels: "TERRAIN" on a small board beside the sand table, "YOUR HEAD" above the stress drill, "SETUPS" on the signpost in the background.

key: Crossing a road without looking. It
name: ch01_crossing_road_without_looking
alt: A man crosses a quiet road many times without looking, shown by faint repeated footprints, until one crossing meets a speeding lorry.
scene: A single wide street-level scene of a two-lane Indian town road beside a tea stall. A young man in his twenties, earphones in, eyes on his phone, steps off the kerb without looking either way. Behind him, drawn faint and ghostly in a long sequence across the zebra crossing, are many earlier copies of himself crossing the same way on quiet days, each with a small green tick floating above, a dozen of them stretching back toward the tea stall. In the current moment, on the right side of the frame, a heavy goods lorry painted with bright tassels is coming fast round the bend, headlights on, horn lines drawn in the air, and the driver's alarmed face visible through the windscreen. The man has not noticed; the tea-stall owner in a vest has dropped his kettle and is shouting with an outstretched arm. A small scoreboard on the tea-stall wall shows many ticks and one large red cross, with the cross clearly far bigger than all the ticks together. Afternoon light, dust kicked up by the lorry, tense, frozen-moment mood. Labels: "WORKED 99 TIMES" above the ghostly crossings, "THE ONE TIME" beside the lorry.

key: Flip a coin that lands heads 55%
name: ch02_coin_three_tails_suspicion
alt: A man glares suspiciously at a coin after three tails in a row, while a long tally on the wall behind him shows heads still winning overall.
scene: A medium shot inside a small study room at night lit by a desk lamp. A man in his thirties wearing a vest and reading glasses pushed up onto his forehead sits at the desk holding a coin up close to one eye, squinting at it with deep suspicion, as if it must be bent or fake. On the desk in front of him three coins lie in a row all showing tails, with a magnifying glass and a small screwdriver beside them as if he is about to take the coin apart. Behind him, the wall is covered with a long hand-drawn tally chart on chart paper with hundreds of marks in two rows; the heads row is visibly longer than the tails row, and scattered through the tails row are several little circled clusters of three tails in a row, showing that the same streak has happened many times before. A thin arrow from his current three-tail row points to one of the many circled clusters on the wall, showing it is just one more of them. A cup of chai cools at his elbow. Warm lamplight on the desk, the wall slightly dimmer, gently humorous mood. Labels: "IS IT BROKEN?" in a thought bubble above his head, "55% HEADS" at the top of the wall tally.

key: The price is a scoreboard of
name: ch03_expectations_scoreboard
alt: A stadium scoreboard shows a great score of 79 against an expected 100, and the crowd groans even though 79 is a strong result.
scene: A wide view of a packed cricket stadium at dusk under floodlights, seen from high in the stands. The giant electronic scoreboard at the far end fills the upper half of the frame with two big rows: the top row reads "EXPECTED 100" and the bottom row reads "ACTUAL 79". In the foreground, rows of spectators who had painted faces and flags ready for celebration now slump; a man in a team jersey covers his face, a woman lowers a half-raised banner, a child looks confused at his father. On the field below, a batsman raises his bat for a fine innings, clearly a good performance, but the applause is thin. Along the bottom of the scoreboard a small ticker-style bar with a downward red arrow shows the mood falling. A thin dotted line runs from the gap between the two numbers on the board to the slumping crowd, showing that the reaction comes from the gap, not the score. Bright white floodlights against a purple evening sky, disappointed, deflated atmosphere. Labels: "GREAT FACT" pointing to the batsman on the field, "DISAPPOINTING NEWS" pointing to the crowd in the stands.

key: A ball bouncing between floor and
name: ch03_ball_floor_ceiling_buyer
alt: A ball bounces between floor and ceiling in a room, and a man reaches up to grab it just as it touches the ceiling and is about to fall.
scene: A side view into a tall, empty, whitewashed room like a school gym, drawn as a cross-section so the floor and ceiling are both clearly visible as thick horizontal bands. A bright red rubber ball is shown in a repeating zig-zag path, faint copies of it marking its earlier bounces from floor to ceiling and back, left to right across the room, with curved motion lines. At the right side, the ball is at the very top, just kissing the ceiling, with a small impact star. Directly below it, a cheerful man in his thirties in a business shirt stands on a wooden stool on tiptoe, arms stretched high, grabbing the ball at that exact moment with a delighted face, money note in his other hand as if paying for it. A dashed arrow from the ball curves sharply downward toward the floor, showing where it will go next, and a small shadow on the floor shows its landing spot. In the left background, a calm older woman sits on a bench waiting near the floor with open hands. Even, clean daylight from high windows, a gently comic mood. Labels: "CEILING" along the top band, "FLOOR" along the bottom band, "BUYS HERE" next to the man on the stool.

key: Draw a wavy line on paper, then tilt
name: ch03_wavy_line_tilted_page
alt: The same wavy line drawn on a sheet of paper is shown flat and then with the page tilted upward, the waves unchanged and only their direction rising.
scene: A two-step illustration on a wooden desk seen from above at a slight angle, divided into left and right halves. LEFT half: a sheet of plain white paper lies flat and straight; a hand holding a pencil has just drawn a long, regular wavy line across it from left to right, with a faint straight horizontal guideline running through the middle of the waves. RIGHT half: the same sheet, with the same wavy line exactly copied, is now being tilted by two hands so that the right edge is raised; the guideline now slopes upward, and the waves ride along that rising line. Small matching numbers 1, 2, 3 mark the same three wave crests in both halves to show they are unchanged in size and shape; a little ruler lies beside each to measure the wave height, reading the same. A curved arrow between the halves shows the tilting movement. Pencils, an eraser and a cup of tea sit at the desk edges. Clean, soft daylight from a window, a calm teaching mood. Labels: "SAME WAVES" near the numbered crests in the right half, "TILTED LINE" along the sloping guideline.

key: A recipe from a famous chef rarely
name: ch06_chef_recipe_own_kitchen
alt: A home cook in a small kitchen tries a famous chef's recipe again and again, noting what went wrong and changing one thing each time until it fits her oven.
scene: A cosy small Indian home kitchen seen from the doorway, a gas stove on the left, a small countertop oven in the middle and a window with a steel grille on the right. A woman in her thirties in a printed cotton salwar and an apron, hair tied up, stands at the counter tasting a spoonful with one eye half-closed, concentrating. Taped to the wall above the counter is a glossy recipe card with a chef's hat drawn on it, and beside it a row of four handwritten notes on sticky paper, each with a small sketch of the dish: the first burnt black, the second sunken, the third almost right, the fourth perfect with a smiley face. Each note has one short line crossed out and one changed, such as a lower oven dial sketched on it. On the counter, four plates in a row show the same four attempts left to right, improving. A curved looping arrow runs from the oven to the tasting spoon to the notes and back to the oven, showing the cycle. A notebook titled "MY VERSION" lies open next to her. Warm evening light from the window and the soft blue glow of the stove flame, homely, patient mood. Labels: "COOK, TASTE, FIX" along the looping arrow.

key: A swimmer in a river. The index is the
name: ch06_swimmer_current_lane
alt: Swimmers race in roped lanes across a flowing river; one swims with the current easily while another fights upstream.
scene: A wide aerial view of a broad, fast-flowing river from above and slightly to one side, with long white arrows painted on the water surface all pointing downstream to the right, showing the current. Floating rope lines with red and white buoys divide the river into several lanes running along its length, like a swimming pool laid on the river. In one lane in the foreground, a strong swimmer in a blue cap is labouring upstream against the arrows, splashing hard, face strained, making only a little progress shown by a short trail of bubbles behind him. In the next lane, a second swimmer in an orange cap glides easily downstream with the current, relaxed strokes, a long wake behind her, already far ahead. On the riverbank a small crowd of spectators watches, and a referee in a white cap stands on a wooden jetty with a whistle. Bright midday sun glittering on the water, lush green banks, energetic mood. Labels: "INDEX = CURRENT" on the riverbank near the arrows, "SECTOR = LANE" on a buoy line, "STOCK = SWIMMER" next to the orange-capped swimmer.

key: Copying trades is like following a
name: ch06_satnav_never_learn_streets
alt: A driver arrives everywhere by following a phone map, but when the screen goes dark he sits lost at an unknown junction.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves inside the same small car in a crowded Indian city. LEFT panel: a young man in his twenties in a polo shirt drives relaxed, eyes glued to a phone mounted on the dashboard that shows a bright blue route line and a big arrow; outside the windscreen the streets, shop signs and a temple gate blur past unnoticed, and a small flag on the phone map shows the destination reached with a tick. RIGHT panel: the same man at night at a busy five-way junction, the phone on the dashboard now black with a tiny empty-battery icon, his hands off the wheel, turning his head anxiously in every direction; around the car, roads branch off under unfamiliar signboards with no clear text, auto-rickshaws honking past, and a confused question mark floats above his head. On the passenger seat a paper city map lies folded and unopened. Daylight with cheerful bright colours on the left, darker, tense streetlight orange on the right. Labels: "ARRIVES" at the top of the left panel, "LOST" at the top of the right panel.

key: A chart pattern works the same way
name: ch06_forecast_seventy_percent_days
alt: A weather forecaster's wall shows ten days all forecast at 70 percent rain, and roughly seven of them turned out rainy and three dry.
scene: A medium shot inside a small weather office with a large wall calendar of ten big square days arranged in two rows of five. Every square has the same printed forecast at the top, a small cloud with "70%" next to it. Below each forecast, a sticker shows what actually happened: seven squares have a rain-cloud sticker with blue drops, three squares have a bright sun sticker, scattered among the days. A middle-aged meteorologist in a white shirt and lanyard, spectacles on her nose, stands pointing a long ruler at the whole calendar, not at any single day, with a calm, satisfied expression. Beside her a young intern in a T-shirt jabs a finger angrily at one of the sunny squares, mouth open in protest, as if that day proves the forecast wrong. A curly bracket spans all ten squares and leads to a small tally on a whiteboard showing seven rain marks against three sun marks. A window behind shows a cloudy sky and a tree swaying. Soft overcast light, light-hearted teaching mood. Labels: "WRONG?" in a speech bubble from the intern, "7 OF 10" beside the tally on the whiteboard.

key: A credit spread is like selling
name: ch06_insurance_vs_lottery_ticket
alt: On the left an insurance seller collects small premiums with a backup policy capping her loss; on the right a buyer holds a cheap ticket with a large possible payout.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a neat insurance office counter where a calm woman in her forties in a blue blazer collects a few small coins from a line of customers holding umbrella-shaped policy cards; each coin drops into her jar labelled with a small plus sign. Behind her stands a tall steel safe, and fixed to the wall is a framed backup policy with a thick red horizontal line drawn across a graph of possible losses, the line marking where her loss stops. Outside her window a small storm cloud gathers, but a sturdy umbrella held by a larger figure in a grey suit shelters her desk, the backup insurer. RIGHT panel: a cheerful young man at a small roadside lottery kiosk hands over one small coin for a ticket; a dotted outline of the coin shows it as all he can lose, while a large glowing bubble above the ticket shows a big pile of money as the possible payout, many times bigger. Bright, even light in both halves, steady in the left and hopeful in the right. Labels: "CREDIT SPREAD" at the top of the left panel, "LONG CALL" at the top of the right panel, "LOSS CAPPED" on the red line.

key: Toss a coin 16 times. Getting 11
name: ch06_coin_tossers_lucky_streak
alt: A hall full of people toss coins; one with a lucky streak celebrates and pushes a bigger stake forward just as his next tosses turn to tails.
scene: A wide view of a large community hall with rows of folding tables, about forty people of all ages each tossing a coin and scoring marks on a small slate. Most slates show a mix of ticks and crosses; a few show bad runs, with a dejected aunty resting her chin on her fist. In the foreground centre, one young man in his twenties in a bright yellow shirt stands up on his chair, slate held high showing a long column of heads, punching the air with pride as neighbours clap; a small badge pinned on his shirt says "EXPERT". In front of him on the table he is pushing a much bigger stack of coins forward than before, while a tiny inset strip above his head, like the next frame of a comic, shows his next three tosses landing tails, tails, tails. A thin arrow runs from his lifted stack to the inset. In the background, a large bell curve is painted on the wall, with his small portrait in the far tail where only a few people sit. Bright fluorescent hall lighting, buzzing, festive mood with a cautionary twist. Labels: "LUCKY STREAK" above the man on the chair, "BIGGER BET" by the stack he is pushing.

key: A bucket with three holes: no plan
name: ch06_bucket_three_holes
alt: Water poured into a bucket runs out through three holes, and three hands plug the holes one by one until the bucket fills.
scene: A three-step sequence arranged left to right across a courtyard with a hand pump in the background, like frames on a strip, all showing the same steel bucket on a stone floor. FIRST frame: a sweating woman in her thirties in a cotton saree and dupatta tied at the waist pours water from a big brass pot into the bucket, but three streams jet out of three holes in its sides and run away across the floor; the bucket stays nearly empty and she looks exasperated. SECOND frame: a hand presses a cork into the first hole, a second hand holds a small compass-shaped plug against the second hole; only one stream still leaks out, and the water level has risen to halfway. THIRD frame: the last hole is sealed with a patch shaped like a notebook page, the bucket is full and still, and the woman stands back smiling, wiping her brow, pot resting on her hip. Small tags hang beside the three holes in the first frame. Bright morning light, puddles reflecting the sky, satisfying mood of a fix. Labels: "NO EXIT PLAN" tag on the first hole, "WRONG DIRECTION" tag on the second hole, "NO JOURNAL" tag on the third hole.

key: A ball bouncing down a staircase. Each
name: ch06_ball_bouncing_down_stairs
alt: A ball bounces down a staircase in similar arcs while people stand on the steps holding catching nets at the measured spots where it is expected to land.
scene: A side view of a long stone staircase descending from upper left to lower right, like old ghat steps beside a river. A bright orange ball is caught mid-journey: faint copies of it trace a series of similar arcs, each bounce a little like the last, landing near the front edge of one step after another. Along the side wall a painter has marked neat measuring ticks at the landing spots, and a few of these marks are coloured gold, labelled with small ratios such as "0.618". On three of those gold-marked steps stand people waiting with butterfly-style nets and cloth bags open, a shopkeeper in a vest, a college student and an older man with a walking stick, all looking up at the ball and leaning toward the same marked spots. At the top of the stairs a boy in a school uniform who dropped the ball watches with hands on his knees. A dotted line projects the next arc ahead of the ball to the next gold mark, showing the guess before it happens. Late afternoon light raking across the steps, long soft shadows, playful but attentive mood. Labels: "NEXT LANDING?" by the dotted arc, "WATCHED LEVEL" next to the gold marks.

key: A taxi meter. If the ride really is
name: ch06_taxi_ride_heading_somewhere
alt: A taxi on a straight highway runs up a growing fare, while the same taxi circling a roundabout only ever charges the starting flag-fall.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves showing a black-and-yellow Indian city taxi from above at a high angle. LEFT panel: the taxi drives along a long straight highway toward a city skyline on the horizon, a big round meter inset beside it showing the fare climbing with each kilometre marker it passes. A passenger in an office shirt leans back calmly. Behind the taxi, two faded earlier copies of the same passenger are shown jumping out early, one after a single block with a tiny coin in hand, the other at a pothole, startled, the meter showing only a small amount each time. RIGHT panel: the same taxi going round and round a busy roundabout, its tyre tracks drawing a circle; the meter inset shows only the starting amount and never rises, and the passenger shrugs with an open palm, the destination nowhere in sight. Clear daylight on the left with an open road feeling, slightly hazy traffic light on the right. Labels: "REAL EDGE" at the top of the left panel, "NO EDGE" at the top of the right panel, "FLAG-FALL" on the meter inset in the right panel.

key: Two drivers on the same road. One
name: ch06_two_drivers_rare_bad_day
alt: Two cars travel the same mountain road; the fast one is fine for years until one foggy day, while the slower one stops in time and keeps driving.
scene: A wide view of a winding hill road with hairpin bends, painted white kilometre stones along the edge and a valley drop on the right. Two cars travel the same road in a sequence that reads left to right as passing years, with small calendar pages floating above showing one year after another. On most of the road, sunny and clear, a red sports-style car driven by a confident man in sunglasses races well ahead of a modest white hatchback driven by a careful woman in her forties with both hands on the wheel. At the far right of the scene, in the last year, thick fog has rolled over one sharp bend and a fallen boulder blocks the road. The red car has skidded at the bend, skid marks curling toward the barrier and its bonnet crumpled against the rocks, the driver standing out of it unhurt but stranded, hands on his head. The white hatchback has stopped neatly a few metres before the boulder with plenty of room, hazard lights blinking, ready to drive on once the road is cleared. Bright light on the left fading to grey fog on the right, sobering mood. Labels: "AVERAGE DAY" above the sunny stretch, "RARE BAD DAY" above the foggy bend.

key: A choir of 500 singers (an index)
name: ch07_choir_vs_soloist
alt: A soloist on a small stage is knocked off-key by one shouted heckle, while a large choir hears the same shout and its overall note barely moves.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves inside the same old concert hall with red velvet curtains. LEFT panel: a single soloist, a young man in a kurta with a shawl, stands alone at a microphone; from the side wings a man with a megaphone shouts a loud piece of news, drawn as a jagged lightning-shaped sound bubble, and the soloist's musical notes, shown as a line of floating notes above his head, crash and stay jagged and broken after the shout, his face shocked. RIGHT panel: a huge tiered choir of many singers in matching cream robes fills the stage, the same megaphone man shouting the same jagged bubble at them. A few singers in the front row wobble sharp with notes rising, a few on the side wobble flat with notes sinking, and many more in the back simply keep singing, eyes on their sheet music. Above the whole choir, one thick smooth line of notes dips slightly where the shout lands and then drifts back to its original height, drawn with a gentle arrow returning it. Warm stage spotlights, deep shadows in the hall, dramatic but calm mood. Labels: "ONE STOCK" at the top of the left panel, "INDEX" at the top of the right panel, "DRIFTS BACK" next to the returning note line.

key: A Bahamas gap is a flight that lands
name: ch07_smooth_vs_bumpy_flight
alt: Two flights reach the same runway: one glides in smoothly, the other shakes through turbulence while a calm passenger keeps his hands off the emergency exit.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle, each half showing a passenger aircraft approaching the same runway with the same palm-lined airport at the far right edge. LEFT panel: clear blue sky, the plane glides in on a straight dotted path, wheels down, and through a cut-away window a relaxed passenger in a holiday shirt sips juice with a smile. RIGHT panel: dark grey clouds, the same type of plane bumps along a jagged, saw-tooth dotted path with jolt lines around the fuselage, but the jagged path still ends on the same runway. In a large circular inset of the cabin, a nervous young man in a hoodie has half-risen from his seat and is reaching for the red emergency-exit lever beside the wing, eyes wide; next to him an older woman in a pale saree calmly rests her hand on his arm and shakes her head, seatbelt fastened, looking out of the window at the runway lights ahead. A small checkered destination flag sits at the end of both runways. Bright, sunny light on the left, stormy grey with flickering cabin lights on the right, tense but reassuring mood. Labels: "SMOOTH GAP" above the left plane, "BUMPY GAP" above the right plane, "STAY SEATED" beside the emergency lever.

key: The numbers are fixed on the ground
name: ch08_pilot_checklist_on_ground
alt: A pilot fills in a checklist calmly on the ground before take-off, then in flight only glances from the list to the instruments.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a quiet airport apron at dawn, the plane parked with its door open and stairs attached; a pilot in her forties in a white shirt with epaulettes and a captain's cap sits on the bottom step with a clipboard on her knee, carefully writing numbers into a printed checklist with a pen, a cup of tea beside her, the propellers still, a ground crew member leaning on a tug in the background. The checklist rows are drawn as short lines with boxes, and three boxes have numbers written in. RIGHT panel: inside the cockpit in flight, clouds rushing past the windscreen, turbulence lines at the edges, lights blinking on the panel; the same pilot sits upright, one hand on the controls, and the same clipboard is clipped beside the instrument panel. A dotted line connects one number on the clipboard to a matching dial on the instrument panel, and her eyes follow that line, calm and focused. Soft pink dawn light on the left, cool blue cockpit glow on the right, composed, professional mood. Labels: "BEFORE TAKE-OFF" at the top of the left panel, "IN THE AIR" at the top of the right panel.

key: A rumour moving through a crowded hall
name: ch08_rumour_through_hall
alt: A rumour spreads through a hall from the people by the door, who act first, to the middle, to people outside the window who act last.
scene: A high, angled view down into a crowded wedding-style hall with chandeliers, a long buffet along the back wall and a large double door on the left. Near the door, three sharp-eyed guests in smart clothes lean together whispering; a ripple of curved sound lines starts from them, coloured bright, and spreads across the room in widening rings toward the right. The door group is already moving out with plates of the best sweets in their hands, calm and early. In the middle of the hall, a dense crowd of guests has just heard the rumour, the rings reaching them late; they jostle and push toward the buffet all at once, plates tipping, faces anxious, the worst crush. Outside the big window on the right, on the street, a group of people peer in through the glass reading small notice cards and only now begin to run toward the entrance. Back at the door, the first group calmly offers their plates to the latecomers. Numbered circles 1, 2, 3 mark the order in which each group acts. Warm golden chandelier light inside, cool blue street light outside, busy and slightly chaotic mood. Labels: "FIRST" by the door group, "LAST" by the people at the window.

key: A lift that stops at every floor
name: ch08_lift_floors_pullback
alt: A cut-away lift shaft shows a man stepping into the lift when its doors open on a floor it just passed, riding up and leaving one or two floors later.
scene: A cut-away front view of a five-storey building with the front wall removed, showing a glass lift shaft running up the centre and a landing on each floor numbered 1 to 5 on small plates. The lift car is drawn several times as faint ghost copies in a sequence: it rises past floor 2, then drops back a little and opens its doors at floor 2, and a man in his thirties in a light blue office shirt with a laptop bag steps in, one foot over the threshold, calm and unhurried. A curved arrow then carries the lift upward, and the man is shown stepping out at floor 3, and a second faint copy of him stepping out at floor 4, each time with a small satisfied nod. On one floor the lift sails past with doors shut; on that landing the same man stands waiting with his arms folded rather than prising the doors open, a small clock above his head. Little dotted footprints track his path through the building. Bright, even interior light, tidy and orderly mood. Labels: "GET ON" at floor 2 where the doors open, "GET OFF" at floors 3 and 4, "WAIT" beside the man on the skipped landing.

key: A smoke alarm, a kitchen timer and a
name: ch09_alarm_timer_two_strikes
alt: In a kitchen a cook reacts to a beeping smoke alarm, sets a timer to stop waiting, and after a second alarm decides the kitchen really is on fire.
scene: A medium-wide view of a busy Indian home kitchen with a pressure cooker on the gas, steel utensils on hooks and a smoke alarm on the ceiling. Three objects are drawn with bold outlines as the heroes of the scene: the round ceiling smoke alarm, blinking red with sound lines; a white egg-shaped kitchen timer on the counter with its dial turning; and a small chalk slate hung by the fridge with two tally strokes. A middle-aged man in a vest and checked lungi, a towel over his shoulder, stands in the middle of the room: one hand reaches up toward the alarm as if answering it, the other is twisting the timer. Over the stove, a light wisp of smoke curls from a pan. On the slate, the second tally stroke has just been drawn and a stick of chalk is still in the air beside it, and the man's face has changed from casual to serious, eyebrows raised, as he finally reaches for the fire extinguisher by the door. A thin arrow links alarm, timer and slate in order. Warm afternoon kitchen light with a faint grey haze near the ceiling, busy, slightly comic mood. Labels: "ACT" beside the smoke alarm, "GIVE UP" beside the timer, "TWO STRIKES" beside the slate.

key: A fisherman with lines out and an alarm
name: ch09_fisherman_rod_bells_reading
alt: A relaxed fisherman reads a book on a jetty with several rods out, each with a little bell, and reels in only the rod whose bell is ringing.
scene: A wide, peaceful view of a wooden jetty jutting into a calm backwater lined with coconut palms. Four fishing rods are fixed in holders along the edge of the jetty, their lines slanting into the water, and each rod tip carries a small brass bell. A man in his fifties with a grey stubble beard, a white half-sleeve shirt and a folded cotton cap sits in a low folding chair under a small umbrella, reading a thick book with a flask of tea at his side; three of the rods are perfectly still. On the second rod from the left the bell is ringing, drawn with little sound lines, the rod bent under a tug, and the man is shown in a second, slightly transparent overlay pose at that rod, book put face down, reeling in, a small timer clipped to his belt. Behind him, a younger man on the neighbouring jetty stands rigid, staring at the water with tense shoulders and binoculars, no book, no bells, clearly tired. Gentle golden morning light, mist over the backwater, calm and unhurried mood. Labels: "ALERT" beside the ringing bell, "STARING" above the tense neighbour.

key: Knocking on a door. A probe is one knock
name: ch09_knock_vs_lean_on_door
alt: On the left a visitor knocks once and walks away; on the right a heavy man leans his whole weight on the same door, shoving it shut every time it opens a crack.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves showing the same blue painted wooden front door of an old house with a brass knocker and a doormat. LEFT panel: a slim young delivery man in a cap taps the door once with one knuckle, a single small "knock" sound line, then is already turning away down the steps with a parcel, glancing back casually; the door stays shut and still. RIGHT panel: a big, burly man in a brown jacket has put his shoulder and his whole body weight against the door, feet braced on the doormat, face straining. From the inside, shown in a small cut-away window, someone tries to open the door; it opens just a crack of light and is immediately shoved shut again, shown by repeated motion lines and a small looping arrow that goes open, shut, open, shut. Beside the door, a small dial painted on the wall reads "0.00" in the middle, and the needle twitches toward it each time the crack opens, then falls back. Afternoon light with long shadows on the left, heavier shade and tension on the right. Labels: "PROBE" at the top of the left panel, "REAL SELLING" at the top of the right panel.

key: A tide gauge versus individual waves
name: ch09_tide_gauge_vs_waves
alt: Waves splash above a mark on a harbour tide pole, while a slow-moving tide line on the same pole shows the water is actually going out.
scene: A close-medium view of a harbour wall with a tall white tide pole fixed to it, painted with black measuring stripes from bottom to top and a bold red line across the middle. Small waves splash against the pole, and one lively wave has just thrown a spray of water well above the red line, droplets frozen in the air. Behind and beside the spray, two smooth, slow lines drawn as soft blue bands on the pole, one slightly above the other, show where the real water level has been sitting over the last hours; both are clearly below the red line and both have small down-pointing arrows, showing the tide going out. A fisherman in his sixties in a vest and dhoti sits on the harbour wall with his net, ignoring the splash and looking at the slow bands, while a young boy beside him jumps up pointing excitedly at the spray. Moored boats in the background are tilting as they settle onto the mud, confirming low water. Soft late-afternoon light on wet stone, calm, knowing mood. Labels: "JUST A WAVE" beside the spray, "TIDE GOING OUT" beside the two slow bands.

key: A road with a centre line (the 13 mean)
name: ch10_road_centre_line_kerbs
alt: A car swerves gently within its lane on a road with a centre line and two kerbs, while only one car that has lost control hits the kerb.
scene: A straight, top-down view of a long two-lane highway running from the bottom of the frame to the top, a dashed white centre line down the middle and two raised kerbs painted black and yellow along the edges. Several small cars travel up the road one after another, each leaving a faint tyre track: most tracks wobble gently from side to side around the centre line, ordinary swerves that stay comfortably inside the road. Measuring arrows on the left side show the distance from centre line to kerb as one and a half times the size of an ordinary swerve, with a small ruler symbol. Near the top of the frame one red car has lost control: its track swings wildly, tyre smoke puffs, and it bumps up against the right-hand kerb, sparks flying, the driver's startled face visible through the windscreen. Beyond the kerbs, fields of mustard flowers stretch away on both sides. Bright midday sun, clear shadows, orderly mood with one dramatic moment. Labels: "MEAN" along the centre line, "BAND" on each kerb, "LOST CONTROL" beside the red car.

key: A metal detector tested on three beaches
name: ch11_metal_detector_three_beaches
alt: A metal detector beeps over planted coins on one beach, finds nothing on a second, and only on a third, with coins naturally drifting, gives an honest test.
scene: A wide three-panel strip of beaches side by side, separated by thin vertical lines, each panel showing the same man in his forties in a wide-brimmed hat, shorts and a vest sweeping the same metal detector over the sand. Each panel has a cut-away strip of sand at the bottom so the viewer can see what lies underneath. FIRST panel: under every flat, quiet patch of sand a coin has been neatly buried, and in the background a sneaky helper with a small spade is still planting more; the detector beeps with green sound lines and the man grins triumphantly. SECOND panel: the cut-away sand is completely empty, just shells and pebbles, and the detector is silent while the man frowns and shakes it. THIRD panel: coins lie scattered unevenly in the sand, with faint curved arrows showing them drifting slowly along the shore with the waves; the detector beeps over some patches and not others, and the man kneels thoughtfully, digging. Bright seaside sunlight, blue sky with gulls, gently comic and curious mood. Labels: "PLANTED" at the top of the first panel, "EMPTY" at the top of the second panel, "REAL SHORE" at the top of the third panel.

key: A daily squeeze is like boarding a long
name: ch11_long_train_vs_city_bus
alt: A relaxed passenger settles into a long-distance train berth for the whole journey, while another hops on and off a city bus at every stop to check the route.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: inside an Indian long-distance sleeper train compartment, blue berths, a window showing fields and a distant hill rolling past. A woman in her fifties in a comfortable cotton saree has stowed her suitcase under the seat, ticket tucked into her bag, and sits back with a newspaper and a steel tiffin open beside her, perfectly at ease; a small route map above the window shows one long line to a far city with several stations dotted along it that the train will pass. RIGHT panel: a crowded city street with a red city bus at a stop. A young man in a shirt and backpack is shown three times as faint copies, jumping off at one stop, peering at the route board with a worried face, jumping back on, then jumping off again at the next stop, with dotted footprints looping in and out of the bus door; he looks harried and sweaty, his ticket crumpled. Warm, steady light through the train window on the left, harsh noon glare and traffic dust on the right. Labels: "DAILY SQUEEZE" at the top of the left panel, "CITY BUS" at the top of the right panel, "STAY SEATED" beside the woman.

key: Arriving at a party at midnight when
name: ch11_party_at_midnight
alt: A guest arrives in party clothes at midnight as the host stacks chairs, and departing guests happily hand him their half-finished drinks.
scene: A wide view of a rooftop party at midnight in an Indian city, strings of fairy lights drooping, most of the bulbs already switched off. A wall clock on the stairwell door shows both hands at twelve. The host, a tired man in his forties with his sleeves rolled up, is stacking white plastic chairs into a tall tower, while a helper rolls up a carpet and the DJ is packing speakers into a case. In the doorway on the left stands a freshly arrived young man in a shiny new party shirt, hair gelled, holding a gift box, eager and smiling, clearly expecting the party to be just starting. Around him, guests heading out to the stairs, yawning and carrying their shoes, cheerfully push their half-empty glasses into his hands until he is juggling four of them, his smile turning uncertain. A plate of leftover snacks on a table holds only crumbs. Dim, cool light with a few remaining warm bulbs, an end-of-night mood, gently comic. Labels: "LATE ENTRY" above the young man in the doorway, "LEAVING" above the departing guests on the stairs.

key: whether the fire is a burnt toast or a
name: ch11_smoke_alarm_toast_or_fire
alt: The same ceiling smoke alarm beeps identically over a slightly burnt slice of toast and over a real fire, unable to tell the difference.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, with one identical round white smoke alarm drawn on the ceiling at the top of each panel, both blinking red with exactly the same three curved sound lines. LEFT panel: a small apartment breakfast nook in the morning; a toaster pops up one slice of blackened toast, a thin grey wisp of smoke curling up toward the alarm, and a sleepy young woman in pyjamas waves a newspaper at it, mildly annoyed. RIGHT panel: a store room at night where a real fire has started among cardboard boxes, orange flames climbing, thick dark smoke rolling along the ceiling to the same alarm; a man in a night shirt runs toward the door with a bucket, alarmed. Between the two alarms, across the top of the image, a single bracket joins them with a small inset of the alarm's simple insides: just a smoke sensor and a speaker, no eyes and no brain, a question mark beside it. Soft yellow morning light on the left, deep orange and black on the right, a clear contrast in stakes. Labels: "SAME BEEP" on the bracket joining the alarms, "TOAST" under the left panel, "FIRE" under the right panel.

key: The dollar is the tide; most dollar
name: ch11_dollar_tide_lifts_boats
alt: A harbour full of many different boats all rise together on an incoming tide, with a tide pole marking the water level as the one thing that moves them all.
scene: A wide panoramic view of a busy fishing harbour with many different boats moored side by side: a painted wooden fishing boat, a small motor launch, a cargo barge, a sailing dinghy and a rowing boat, each labelled by a small wooden tag with a simple pictogram on it such as a gold bar, a wheat sheaf, an oil drum and a copper coil, to suggest different goods. Faint dotted outlines below each boat show where it sat earlier, lower down, and small upward arrows show all of them rising by the same height together. On the harbour wall at the right stands a tall tide pole with measuring stripes and a large arrow on it pointing up, the water level having climbed visibly. An old harbour master in a white cap and a navy jacket stands beside the pole holding a telescope, looking at a small clipboard showing the tide chart with a narrowing then widening squiggle on it, ready to call out. Gulls circle overhead. Bright early-evening light glinting on the water, a feeling of one big force moving everything at once. Labels: "THE DOLLAR" beside the tide pole, "ALL BOATS RISE" across the water near the boats.

key: Walking on an airport travelator
name: ch11_travelator_with_vs_against
alt: On an airport moving walkway one traveller strides with it easily while another walks against it, toiling and stumbling backward.
scene: A long airport corridor with a moving walkway running from left to right across the frame, large windows behind showing parked aircraft and a bright sky. Chevrons painted on the walkway belt and arrows on its rubber handrail all point to the right, showing the direction it moves. On the upper lane, a businesswoman in her thirties in a trouser suit, pulling a small wheeled bag, strides along with the belt; long motion lines and footprint marks spaced far apart show each step carrying her twice as far, and she looks relaxed, checking her boarding pass. On the lower lane, which runs the same way, a man in his forties with a heavy backpack is stubbornly walking against the belt toward the left; his footprints are crowded close together, sweat flies from his forehead, and a small inset shows him tripping on one step and sliding backward with a startled face. A floor sign with an arrow and a small clock hangs from the ceiling above. Bright, clean terminal lighting, polished floor reflections, light-hearted mood. Labels: "WITH THE TREND" above the woman, "AGAINST IT" above the man.

key: A sticky note on your monitor that says
name: ch12_sticky_note_on_monitor
alt: A trader at a desk glances at a sticky note on his monitor that says which way the river flows today, instead of walking to the window to check.
scene: A medium shot of a home trading desk in a small apartment room, two monitors showing simple price charts with a wavy indicator strip along the bottom of each. Stuck to the bezel of the left monitor is a bright yellow sticky note with a quick hand-drawn sketch of a river flowing downhill from left to right with a downward arrow, and the short words "DOWN TODAY" in marker. A man in his thirties in a T-shirt and track pants sits in an office chair with a mug, glancing at the note while his hand is on the mouse, calm and decided. On the far right of the room a window looks out over a real river in a valley below, flowing in the same direction as the sketch. A faint dotted path on the floor runs from his chair to the window and back, crossed out with a light X, showing the trip he no longer needs to make. A thin dotted line also connects the note to the wavy strip at the bottom of the charts, showing it is the same message printed under every chart. Soft morning daylight from the window mixed with screen glow, calm, organised mood. Labels: "C WAVE" next to the wavy strip under the charts, "NO TRIP" beside the crossed-out path.

key: A car slowing at a junction. Brake
name: ch12_brake_lights_then_turn
alt: A car first shows brake lights approaching a junction, then visibly turns its nose down the side street, while a cyclist behind gets ready and then acts.
scene: A two-step sequence on the same city road seen from slightly above and behind, arranged left to right like two frames, separated by a thin line. FIRST frame: a white hatchback approaches a T-junction with a side street going off to the right, its two red brake lights glowing brightly with small glow rings; a cyclist delivery rider in a red jacket with a box on his carrier follows behind, lifting his head, fingers moving to his own brakes, alert but still going straight. SECOND frame: the same car has its front wheels turned and its nose already pointing down the side street, the body angled, the orange indicator blinking; now the cyclist leans and steers to pass on the left side, decisive, pedalling forward into the gap. Numbered circles mark the frames, 1 above the glowing brake lights and 2 above the turned front wheels. Shops and a banyan tree line the street, a few pedestrians on the footpath. Clear late-afternoon light with warm reflections on the car, alert, practical mood. Labels: "GET READY" beneath the first frame, "ACT" beneath the second frame.

key: Three traffic lights in a row
name: ch12_three_traffic_lights
alt: A sleek sports car waits before three traffic lights in a row; only when all three are green does it go, with a red one meaning a one-way street and an amber one a stuck road.
scene: A three-part strip of the same road scene, side by side, each showing a sleek unbranded silver sports car waiting at a line in front of three traffic lights mounted one after another along the road ahead. FIRST part: all three lights glow green, the road ahead is open, and the car speeds off with motion lines, the driver in sunglasses smiling. SECOND part: the first two lights are green but the third is red, and beyond it a blue one-way sign with a white arrow points back toward the car; a wrong-way symbol on the road shows the car would be driving against traffic, and the driver keeps his hands off the wheel. THIRD part: two lights green and one stuck on amber, and beyond it the road is jammed with stationary lorries and auto-rickshaws, horns silent, a clock showing time passing; the driver drums his fingers, waiting. Tiny letters A, B and C sit under the three lights on each post. Bright clear daylight, crisp shadows, decision-making mood. Labels: "GO" over the first part, "WRONG WAY" over the second part, "NOT MOVING YET" over the third part.

key: Someone walking up a staircase with a
name: ch14_heavy_bag_staircase_shuffle
alt: A man carrying a heavy bag up a staircase shuffles back half a step three times, but is only believed to be going down when he steps below his last step.
scene: A side view of a long, wide outdoor staircase climbing from lower left to upper right, like the steps up to a hilltop temple, with a painted handrail. A man in his forties in a sweat-darkened kurta carries a heavy jute sack over one shoulder, climbing upward. Around his current step, faint ghost copies of his feet show three small backward shuffles of half a step each, with little curved arrows going back and then forward again, while his body stays leaning uphill and his eyes stay on the top. A thin dashed horizontal line is drawn at the edge of the last full step he stood firmly on, just beneath his heels. On the lower right, a separate small inset shows the decisive case: his foot actually stepping down below that dashed line onto the step beneath, the sack slipping, with a bold red down arrow. Two onlookers stand at the side of the stairs: a jumpy young man pointing down at every shuffle, shouting, and a calm older woman with her eyes on the dashed line. Bright morning sun on the stone steps, gentle effort-filled mood. Labels: "JUST A SHUFFLE" beside the half-steps, "LAST STEP" on the dashed line, "TURNED" in the inset.

key: A coastline looks jagged from a plane
name: ch14_coastline_plane_and_beach
alt: The same jagged pattern of bays and headlands is seen from an aeroplane window and again in miniature at a child's feet on the beach.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: the view through an oval aeroplane window, a passenger's hand resting on the sill, looking down from high above at a long coastline of bays, headlands and inlets, the shore edge drawn as a crinkled jagged line with a deep blue sea and green land. RIGHT panel: a close view on the sand at the water's edge, a little girl of about seven in a frock squats down with a bucket, and at her feet the tiny edge of the wet sand forms a miniature version of the very same jagged pattern of small bays and headlands, a few centimetres across, with tiny ripples instead of big waves. A thin dotted outline traces the jagged shape in both panels, matching exactly, with a magnifying-glass icon between them. A small scale bar under each panel shows a large distance on the left and a tiny one on the right. Bright, breezy seaside daylight in both, wonder-filled mood. Labels: "FROM A PLANE" at the top of the left panel, "FROM THE BEACH" at the top of the right panel, "SAME SHAPE" beside the magnifying glass.

key: A thermostat with a dead band
name: ch14_thermostat_dead_band
alt: A room thermostat ignores the first cold reading and switches the heater on only after three cold readings in a row, staying on until three warm readings.
scene: A medium shot of a living room wall in a hill-station cottage, with a large round wall thermostat in the centre, a small oil heater on the floor below it and a window showing snowy pine trees. Running along the wall from left to right above the thermostat is a strip of ten small thermometer readings like a timeline, each a little thermometer icon coloured blue for cold or red for warm. The first single blue reading is followed by a red one, and the thermostat's switch stays still; then three blue readings in a row are bracketed together, and at that moment a curved arrow points to the thermostat flipping to "HEAT", the heater glowing orange. Further along, a single red reading does nothing, and only after three red readings in a row does a second bracket flip the switch to "COOL" and the heater fade. An elderly man in a woollen cap and shawl sits in an armchair with tea, reading, not touching the thermostat at all. A small inset shows the switch has only two positions and never sits in between. Cosy warm interior light against the cool blue window, steady, calm mood. Labels: "THREE IN A ROW" above each bracket, "ALWAYS IN" beside the inset.

key: He compares these swing trades to
name: ch14_rental_flat_vs_running_building
alt: One owner relaxes while a management company looks after his rented flat; another runs a whole building himself, fixing pipes and collecting rent at all hours.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves showing the same mid-rise apartment building in an Indian city with balconies and potted plants. LEFT panel: a relaxed man in his fifties in a crisp shirt sits on a park bench across the street reading a newspaper, a cup of coffee beside him; at the building, a woman from a management company in a uniform polo with a clipboard is handing keys to a smiling tenant family, and a plumber in overalls walks in with a toolbox, all handled without him. A small phone on his bench shows a single message with a tick. RIGHT panel: a frazzled man in his thirties in a vest, hair messy, is doing everything himself: on a ladder fixing a dripping pipe, then shown as smaller copies running up the stairs with a gas cylinder, knocking on a door with a rent book, and answering a ringing phone with a wrench still in his hand; a clock on the wall reads late at night and the building windows are dark. Calm, sunny morning light on the left, harsh yellow bulb light and night on the right. Labels: "SWING TRADE" at the top of the left panel, "INTRADAY" at the top of the right panel.

key: Every dish looks perfect because the
name: ch14_photo_menu_best_plate
alt: A restaurant photo menu shows a perfect dish while a photographer chose it from a table of ordinary and messy plates hidden behind the camera.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a diner in his twenties at a roadside dhaba table, holding up a large laminated photo menu showing a gleaming, perfectly arranged plate of biryani with a garnish of fried onions and a boiled egg, his eyes wide and hungry; on the menu, smaller pictures of other perfect dishes surround it. RIGHT panel: behind the scenes in the dhaba kitchen during a photo shoot, a photographer in a cap crouches with a camera on a tripod aimed at one single perfect plate under a bright lamp; behind him, out of the camera's view, a long steel counter holds many other plates of the same dish, some lopsided, some spilled, one slightly burnt, one half-eaten by a cat sneaking onto the counter. A dashed triangle from the camera lens shows the narrow view that captures only the perfect plate. The cook in a white vest and cap stands with arms crossed beside the ordinary plates, amused. name: ch14_u_turn_in_doorway
alt: In a long corridor, a man turning around right in a doorway looks deliberate, while another man turning around in the middle of the corridor looks like he is just hesitating.
scene: A long office corridor seen from one end in deep perspective, beige walls, a patterned floor and three open doorways along the left wall leading into bright rooms. Faint footprints on the floor show that many past walkers have turned around right at the doorways, with little U-shaped arrows clustered on the floor at each threshold. In the foreground at the first doorway, a man in his thirties in a tie and rolled sleeves is mid-U-turn exactly on the threshold, one hand on the door frame, his body clearly swinging back the way he came, a firm, decided expression; a bold green U-turn arrow is drawn under his feet. Further down, in the empty middle of the corridor between doorways, a second man in a cardigan has also half-turned, but he is glancing over his shoulder with a puzzled look, a question mark above him and a faint, dotted, uncertain U-turn arrow under his feet, clearly not committed. A sign above the first doorway carries a small level-marker icon. Even, cool office lighting with warm light spilling from the doorways, observational mood. Labels: "PIVOT" above the first doorway, "U-TURN" beside the man in the doorway.
